outline.title: Ada and the Eagle's Big Swim
outline.logline: Ada wants to help the eagle live in the ocean and runs bathtub tests until she finds the secret that lets the eagle's third try work.
outline.theme: testing ideas until you find what works

characters.name: Ada
characters.description: A six-year-old who loves oceans and submarines and wants to help the eagle make the water his home by testing what it needs.

characters.name: Eagle
characters.description: A bird who spots the ocean and decides to make it his new home.

beats.title: Ada at the tub
beats.summary: Ada fills her bathtub and sends a small submarine under the bubbles. She hears an eagle call from the window and sees him land on the shore.

beats.title: New planet below
beats.summary: The eagle tells himself the water is a new planet he will live on. He takes a deep breath and dives for the first time.

beats.title: First try
beats.summary: The eagle kicks and flaps but meets nothing to push against. He pops up and tries again the same way while Ada watches.

beats.title: Second try
beats.summary: The eagle dives once more, flaps hard, and meets the same empty push. Ada decides she must test what the ocean planet needs so she can help.

beats.title: Bathtub test
beats.summary: Ada puts a jar over a toy submarine in the tub so a pocket of air stays inside. She sees the air lets the toy rise and move.

beats.title: Ada brings the air
beats.summary: Ada fills a jar with air from her test, carries it to the shore, and sets it in the water near the eagle so a pocket forms.

beats.title: Third try works
beats.summary: The eagle dives a third time, reaches the air Ada placed, and uses it to push with his wings. He stays and calls that the ocean planet works after all while Ada watches from the edge.

pages.text: Bubbles rise over the submarine in the tub. Through the window an eagle lands. Ada notices and draws nearer.
A deep breath fills him. The ocean waits as his home. He dives straight down.
Kicks and flaps bring no forward push. He pops up to the surface. The eagle beats his wings harder.
The eagle tries the same dive again. Still the water gives no help. Ada wonders what might change it.
At home Ada sets a jar over the toy sub. Air stays trapped in the water. She watches it rise and slide.
Ada carries the jar along the path. The air pocket stays inside. Closer and closer it travels.
The jar touches the waves. A pocket of air opens near the eagle. Ada waits to see what follows.
Wings reach the air pocket. He pushes and holds his place. The sea works for him at last.
